name: Container & Kubernetes Security
tagline: Defending your own clusters: image scanning, SBOM, runtime detection, CIS posture, admission policy, Sigstore signing, and offensive lab checks.

tools.name: Trivy
tools.desc: Aqua Security's comprehensive scanner covering container images, filesystems, git repos, VMs, and Kubernetes; detects CVEs, misconfigurations, secrets, and licenses from one binary.
tools.when: Gate every image build in CI and scan at push time; add trivy-operator (or Kubescape) for in-cluster image monitoring.

tools.name: Grype
tools.desc: Anchore's fast vulnerability scanner for images, filesystems, and SBOMs; pairs with Syft and adds EPSS, KEV, and OpenVEX filtering to prioritize real risk.
tools.when: Speed-first CI scans, or scan an SBOM you already generated instead of re-pulling and re-analyzing the image.

tools.name: Clair
tools.desc: Quay/Red Hat's v4 vulnerability database server for registries: ingests manifests and exposes a gRPC API that clairctl, clair-hook, or admission controllers query for container-layer CVE data.
tools.when: Deploy next to Quay (or your own registry) for server-side scanning of every pushed image instead of one-off CI scans.

tools.name: Anchore (Enterprise)
tools.desc: Commercial policy-and-compliance platform built on the Grype/Syft engine with admission control (anchore-admission-controller) and scheduled registry scanning; the legacy open-source anchore-engine CLI is deprecated.
tools.when: When you need continuous registry posture, feeds/webhooks, and audited policy gates as a platform rather than a single binary.
tools.install: helm repo add anchore https://charts.anchore.io && helm install anchore anchore/anchore-enterprise

tools.name: Docker Scout
tools.desc: Docker's image analyzer for CVEs, provenance, and supply-chain compliance; highlights CISA KEV reachability and suggests base-image/model upgrades, integrated into Docker Desktop and CI.
tools.when: Fastest starting point for teams already on Docker — compare images, audit a registry, and enforce policies without another platform.

tools.name: Snyk Container
tools.desc: Snyk's container scanning CLI ('snyk container test') covering images plus Kubernetes/IaC config, with base-image upgrade paths and registry/workspace integration.
tools.when: Teams already using Snyk for SCA/app-sec want container coverage in the same console and policy engine.

tools.name: hadolint
tools.desc: Haskell Dockerfile linter that parses the Dockerfile AST and applies best-practice rules, delegating inline shell checks to ShellCheck (DL- and SC-prefixed findings).
tools.when: Lint Dockerfiles in CI to catch untagged images, root users, and unsafe RUN commands before the image is ever built.

tools.name: dockle
tools.desc: Container image linter that audits the built image against CIS Docker image checkpoints and best practices (non-root user, HEALTHCHECK, setuid/setgid files, content trust).
tools.when: Audit the built image itself, complementing Dockerfile lint, right before pushing to a production registry.

tools.name: Syft
tools.desc: Generates SBOMs for container images, filesystems, and archives in CycloneDX, SPDX, and Syft JSON; feeds Grype directly and supports signed in-toto attestations.
tools.when: Produce a machine-readable dependency inventory at build time and ship it with the image to prove supply-chain provenance.

tools.name: CycloneDX CLI
tools.desc: OWASP CycloneDX CLI to validate, merge, diff, convert, sign, and verify CycloneDX and SPDX BOMs; exits non-zero on invalid input for CI gating.
tools.when: Normalize third-party vendor SBOMs into one format, diff releases to catch dependency drift, or enforce schema-valid BOMs in the pipeline.

tools.name: sbomqs
tools.desc: Interlynk's SBOM quality & compliance scorer: grades SPDX/CycloneDX BOMs on completeness, licensing, relationships, and format correctness, then filters by quality score.
tools.when: Score vendor-supplied and generated SBOMs in CI so you can reject 'good enough' BOMs and see which tooling produces trustworthy output.

tools.name: Cosign
tools.desc: Sigstore CLI to sign and verify images, blobs, and SBOM attestations with keyless (OIDC) or key-based signatures stored as OCI artifacts, backed by the Rekor transparency log.
tools.when: Sign every image in CI and verify at admission time (Kyverno, Gatekeeper, or the sigstore policy controller) to stop unsigned/mutated image pulls.

tools.name: Notation
tools.desc: CNCF Notary Project CLI (OCI 1.1 signatures) for signing and verifying artifacts with X.509/SPIFFE certificates; keeps signatures as native OCI artifacts and integrates with Azure/AWS KMS signers.
tools.when: Enterprise environments that already run X.509 PKI/KMS and want cert-managed signing rather than Sigstore's ephemeral, keyless model.

tools.name: Sigstore Policy Controller
tools.desc: Sigstore's admission controller that verifies signatures and attestations on every pod creation, mutating the request to enforce trust policies cluster-wide.
tools.when: Cluster-wide 'only signed/attested images run here' enforcement as an image-policy layer, complementary to schema-style admission policies like Kyverno.
tools.install: helm repo add sigstore https://sigstore.github.io/helm-charts && helm install policy-controller sigstore/policy-controller -n cosign-system --create-namespace

tools.name: Rekor CLI
tools.desc: Query and verify entries in the Rekor transparency log (DSSE/tekton/blob/cosign types): confirm a signature was logged at a point in time and detect tampered/duplicate entries.
tools.when: Forensic checks that complement signature verification — prove an artifact existed in the log, correlate with incident timelines, or audit your own signing records.

tools.name: Distroless
tools.desc: Google's minimal base images with no shell, package managers, or runtimes — static, cc, and Debian variants with nonroot tags that slash attack surface and image size.
tools.when: Production images that never need a shell: shift all debugging to the builder stage or sidecars and run the runtime stage as non-root by default.

tools.name: Wolfi
tools.desc: Chainguard's apk-based, no-glibc-bloat OS purpose-built for containers — the upstream of hardened Chainguard images, reproducibly assembled with apko into slim distroless-style images.
tools.when: Teams needing a lean, fully open-source base where you still install apk packages and build tools inside multi-stage builds without bloating the runtime image.

tools.name: kube-bench
tools.desc: Aqua's Go tool that runs the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark against control plane, etcd, and worker node configuration, matched to the running Kubernetes version.
tools.when: Validate a specific hardened baseline after cluster upgrades, node onboarding, or as a scheduled per-node job.

tools.name: docker-bench-security
tools.desc: Docker's CIS Docker Benchmark script auditing the Docker/containerd host, daemon, and running containers against dozens of best-practice checks.
tools.when: Harden and periodically re-audit the container host on worker nodes after workloads are deployed; quick compliance readout for a single host.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/docker/docker-bench-security.git && cd docker-bench-security && sudo sh docker-bench-security.sh

tools.name: Kubescape
tools.desc: CNCF-incubating Kubernetes security platform scanning clusters, manifests, Helm charts, git repos, and images against CIS, NSA-CISA, and MITRE ATT&CK; operator mode adds continuous posture and eBPF runtime.
tools.when: First full-posture sweep of a cluster and as a CI gate on manifests; install the operator for continuous compliance monitoring.

tools.name: Popeye
tools.desc: Read-only live-cluster sanitizer that lints deployed workloads for misconfigurations, dead resources, port mismatches, and missing probes, scoring overall cluster health.
tools.when: Periodic 'wide-open' sweep to catch drift and operational debt that static manifest review misses.

tools.name: kube-linter
tools.desc: StackRox (Red Hat) static analyzer for Kubernetes YAML and Helm charts with 40+ built-in checks (privileged containers, insecure service types, missing resource limits) and SARIF output for CI.
tools.when: Pre-deploy linting in CI — catch risky manifests before apply, complementing runtime posture and admission checks.

tools.name: kubeaudit
tools.desc: Audits manifests and live clusters against security controls (privileged, hostNetwork, capabilities, allowPrivilegeEscalation) and can auto-fix them; repo is archived and the brew formula deprecated as of 2025.
tools.when: Only where an existing pipeline integrates its autofix mode; otherwise prefer kube-linter + kube-bench for actively maintained coverage.

tools.name: OPA Gatekeeper
tools.desc: CNCF policy controller that enforces Rego-based policy through constraint templates and constraints, with admission webhooks, audit, and mutation support.
tools.when: Enforce registry allowlists, required labels, and security-context rules at admission when you already know Rego or want the largest policy ecosystem.

tools.name: Kyverno
tools.desc: CNCF-graduated Kubernetes-native policy engine using YAML (no new language) to validate, mutate, generate, and clean up resources; verifies image signatures via cosign.
tools.when: Teams that prefer familiar YAML and want mutation, image verification, and policy-as-a-resource without learning Rego.
tools.install: helm repo add kyverno https://kyverno.github.io/helm-charts && helm install kyverno kyverno/kyverno -n kyverno --create-namespace

tools.name: Polaris
tools.desc: Fairwinds policy-as-code with 30+ built-in checks across security, networking, reliability, and efficiency; runs as a dashboard, CI CLI, or mutating admission webhook.
tools.when: Drop-in baseline enforcement with a visible compliance dashboard when full OPA or Kyverno is overkill.

tools.name: Conftest
tools.desc: Tests Kubernetes manifests, Helm values, Terraform, and CUE against Rego policies from the CLI; CI-friendly and shares the same policy language as OPA Gatekeeper.
tools.when: Control-plane-free policy checks in pre-commit/CI, or validate the exact Rego you will enforce with Gatekeeper before installing anything.

tools.name: Cilium
tools.desc: eBPF-based CNI enforcing Kubernetes NetworkPolicy and extended CiliumNetworkPolicy with identity-based rules (no IP juggling), plus Hubble for policy-aware flow observability.
tools.when: Strict workload micro-segmentation with per-L4/L7 rules and visibility; it replaces your CNI, so plan a rollout, not a drop-in patch.
tools.install: helm repo add cilium https://helm.cilium.io && helm install cilium cilium/cilium --namespace kube-system

tools.name: Calico
tools.desc: Project Calico/Tigera CNI delivering the Kubernetes NetworkPolicy API plus GlobalNetworkPolicy and host-endpoint policy for traffic entering/leaving nodes.
tools.when: Clusters already on Calico, or when you need global (not just namespace-scoped) network policy that covers host endpoints.

tools.name: kube-hunter
tools.desc: Legacy Aqua pen-test tool that finds cluster weaknesses from an attacker's perspective (exposed dashboards, leaked secrets, weak RBAC); officially no longer under active development.
tools.when: Offense-style spot check on a cluster you own; treat findings as a starting list since it is not actively maintained.

tools.name: Falco
tools.desc: CNCF-graduated kernel monitoring agent (eBPF or driver) that watches syscalls enriched with container and Kubernetes metadata, alerting via a flexible rules engine.
tools.when: Deploy on every production node for real-time detection of shells in containers, privileged pods, and sensitive-file access.
tools.install: helm repo add falcosecurity https://falcosecurity.github.io/charts && helm install falco falcosecurity/falco

tools.name: Tetragon
tools.desc: Cilium's eBPF-based runtime security and observability with no userspace for traffic paths: policy-driven tracing of syscalls and network events, plus kubectl-level enrichment.
tools.when: High-throughput, eBPF-first detection with built-in network insights and lower operational moving parts than a driver-based agent.
tools.install: helm repo add cilium https://helm.cilium.io && helm install tetragon cilium/tetragon -n kube-system

tools.name: rbac-lookup
tools.desc: Fairwinds CLI that reverses RBAC: give it a user, service account, or group and it prints every Role/ClusterRole bound to that identity, resolving the bindings for you.
tools.when: Audit 'what can this identity actually do?' across namespaces — the fastest path from a SA name to a least-privilege review.

tools.name: kubectl auth can-i
tools.desc: Built-in kubectl authorization self-check; 'kubectl auth can-i --list -A' dumps the full permission matrix for the current context in one shot.
tools.when: Zero-install RBAC sanity checks in an incident or review loop — verify a spyed SA cannot escalate before trusting it.

tools.name: Trivy Action
tools.desc: aquasecurity/trivy-action wraps Trivy in GitHub Actions for image, filesystem, config, and SBOM scans with severity gates and SARIF upload to code scanning.
tools.when: Per-PR image/filesystem scanning that fails the build above a severity threshold and feeds findings into GitHub Security tab.

tools.name: Anchore Scan Action
tools.desc: anchore/scan-action runs Grype with fine-grained gating (only-fixed, severity cutoff, OpenVEX) and emits SARIF, JSON, or CycloneDX outputs from images, paths, or existing SBOMs.
tools.when: Grype-grounded, license-clean security scanning where you want VEX and fix-availability filters ahead of generic fail-on-high scans.

tools.name: SBOM Action
tools.desc: anchore/sbom-action generates Syft SBOMs in CI, publishing them as release artifacts or GitHub SBOM attestations so downstream scanners (Clair, Grype, Docker Scout) consume them.
tools.when: Attach a CycloneDX/SPDX BOM to every released image git-tag artifact, proving what shipped for audit and supply-chain consumers.

tools.name: Kyverno Policies
tools.desc: Kyverno's community policy library: 130+ tested YAML policies covering Pod Security Standards, image signatures, network policy checks, and compliance presets.
tools.when: Start from a maintained, battle-tested policy set and adapt, rather than authoring every admission rule from scratch.

tools.name: KubeHound
tools.desc: DataDog's attack-graph engine: a collector ingests cluster RBAC, workload, and network data, then a graph query layer returns BloodHound-style attack paths between assets.
tools.when: Continuously model 'can this workload or identity reach the kubelet/cluster?' — ideal for validating least privilege and red-team path enumeration on your own cluster.

tools.name: KubiScan
tools.desc: CyberArk's RBAC attack-path scanner: lists risky roles, subjects, and clusterrolebindings, and highlights the write-access paths (secrets, exec) an attacker can abuse for cluster takeover.
tools.when: Systematically map RBAC escape routes on clusters you own and gather remediation evidence (which SA grants secret read, exec into pods, etc.).
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/CyberArk/KubiScan.git && cd KubiScan && sudo python3 setup.py install

tools.name: deepce
tools.desc: DEEPCE (Docker Enumeration, Escalation of Privileges and Container Escapes) is a single bash script that enumerates capabilities, mounts, sockets, env, and metadata, then suggests and attempts escapes.
tools.when: Fast assessment of a container you own in a lab/engagement: one script goes from recon to working escape candidates before you write custom exploit code.

tools.name: CDK
tools.desc: Zero-dependency Go container/Kubernetes penetration toolkit: capability evaluation, no-curl/wget binary delivery, and exploits for runC, docker.sock, containerd, etcd tokens, plus tunneling and reverse shells.
tools.when: Post-exploitation payload to drop into minimal/scratch containers where curl and wget are absent but you still need networking, probes, and K8s API calls.
tools.install: Download the release binary from github.com/cdk-team/CDK/releases
